authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates were lower in the defended branch than in the plain attack branch; reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack reference.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.611385, versus 0.049047 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.124462, an absolute reduction of 0.486922 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.671021 to 0.424716, with recovery fraction 0.367060.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: it is unsupported by the evidence.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and exact recovery is unsupported.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is a paired round-4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
